question: What is the primary purpose of MATLAB App Designer?
options: To build a graphical user interface (GUI) with point-and-click controls, so others can use your program without typing MATLAB commands
To automatically optimize your MATLAB code for speed
To convert MATLAB code into another programming language
To generate documentation comments for your functions
explanation: App Designer lets you build a GUI — buttons, sliders, plots, etc. — so a user can run your program by clicking and typing into fields instead of writing MATLAB commands.

Incorrect — App Designer doesn't optimize code performance.
Incorrect — App Designer doesn't translate MATLAB into other languages.
Incorrect — that's not what App Designer is for.

question: In an App Designer app, what is a 'callback'?
options: The code that runs in response to a user action, like clicking a button or moving a slider
The variable that stores the app's title
A comment describing what the app does
The function that closes the app window
explanation: A callback is the block of code tied to a specific component and event — for example, the code that runs when a button is clicked or a slider is moved.
optionExplanations: Correct — a callback is event-response code, e.g. what happens on a button click.
Incorrect — that's just an app property, not a callback.
Incorrect — a comment doesn't execute anything.
Incorrect — closing the app is only one possible callback among many, not the definition of the term.

Rewrite the whole script inside App Designer
Use the appdesigner command with a custom callback
Wrap the number in an input() call

Incorrect — that's a much heavier tool than needed for a single interactive value.

Creating an app interactively only works for plotting code
explanation: Converting a script is a lightweight shortcut for turning a value already in a Live Script into a slider or similar control. Creating an app interactively opens the full App Designer canvas, where you place and wire up any combination of components from a blank layout.
optionExplanations: Correct — one is a lightweight single-value shortcut, the other is a full GUI design workflow.
Incorrect — they serve different scopes of complexity, not the same result.
Incorrect — converting a script actually requires less setup, not more.
Incorrect — creating an app interactively can include any components, not just plots.
